request: Make an original, visually intelligent short explanation of why a DNS change may not appear everywhere immediately. No bland listicle or textbook lecture; help a curious non-engineer understand the actual mechanism.

facts.truth_1: DNS resolvers may temporarily cache previous responses.
facts.truth_2: A record's TTL informs caching duration; resolver policies and other caches can affect observations.
facts.truth_3: Different resolvers may show the old and new answer at the same time during a change.
facts.truth_4: A DNS change is not the same thing as physically moving a website.
